{{Quote|And, of course, there is that corniculate half-bot I revivified for the paltry fee of a double-necked, eight-string quetarra and one more quaint nom de guerre|Zeta Magnus on the cyborg|<ref name="swcw" />}}
A '''horned cyborg''' was reconstructed by the mad [[Geneticist/Legends|genetic]] [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] [[Zeta Magnus]]. Magnus exacted a double-necked eight-string [[quetarra]] and the rights to an alias as payment for his services.<ref name="swcw" />

==Behind the scenes==
In a forum post on the [[Jedi Council Forums]], [[SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story|''SkyeWalkers'']] author [[Abel G. Peña]] revealed that the intended identity of the cyborg is [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]]. The cyborg's description as a "corniculate half-bot" is a reference to Darth Maul's appearance with cybernetic legs and longer horns in the [[Star Wars: Visionaries|''Star Wars: Visionaries'']] comic [[Old Wounds|''Old Wounds'']]. The double-necked quetarra Zeta Magnus receives as payment is a reference to the double-necked electric guitar Darth Maul plays in [[Randy Martinez]]'s "[https://www.randymartinez.art/fullscreen-page/comp-jj1r9r4n/c6038817-ef41-4438-9367-ebbfd89a4215/0/%3Fi%3D0%26p%3Dtp1ia%26s%3Dstyle-jj1r9r5d1 Sith Rocks]" illustration created for [[Celebration IV|Star Wars Celebration IV]]. The alias Zeta Magnus took from the cyborg is intended to be K'am'ir Zaarin, a reference to Darth Maul's alleged birthname "Khameir Sarin" that was supposedly cut from English literary material for [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace'']], but was rumored to be preserved in versions written in other languages.<ref name="JCF">{{JCFCite|url=posts/52250872|board=Literature|thread=Abel G. Peña's "Skyewalkers" and "Lone Wolf"|user=[[Abel G. Peña|Halagad_Ventor]]|date=2015-03-23|time=6:26 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230531204742/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/abel-g-pe%C3%B1as-skyewalkers-and-lone-wolf.50027998/page-6#post-52250872|quote=In the Interludium, there is a complex Easter egg that essentially ended up being contradicted by the TV series. Magnus refers to "that corniculate half-bot I revivified for the paltry fee of a double-necked, eight-string quetarra and one more quaint ''nom de guerre''." If you read this carefully, it is actually a reference to cyborg Darth Maul, who I'd already previously referred to in "The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War": the parts about a "corniculate half-bot" referred to his appearance in the comic "Old Wounds"; the payment of a "double-necked, eight-string quetarra" was a reference to Randy Martinez's "Sith Rocks" illustration and "one more quaint ''nom de guerre''" was a reference to the fact that Magnus had taken the alias "K'am'ir Zaarin" (a.k.a. Khameir Sarin, the supposed birthname of Darth Maul cut from official Episode I English materials but supposedly printed in some official foreign translations).}}</ref>
